name: Mung Bean
description: Mung beans represent the prepared edible seeds of Vigna radiata, serving as an advanced nutrient-dense legume superfood characterized by a highly digestible protein-starch hydro-matrix. Structurally, the cotyledon tissue packages an optimal ratio of globulin and albumin storage proteins alongside structured, slowly digestible amylose polymers and complex non-starch polysaccharides. The unique genetic profile of this legume exhibits a significantly lower concentration of gas-producing alpha-galactoside oligosaccharides compared to other members of the Fabaceae family. This structural advantage is paired with a potent polyphenolic profile dominated by the flavone C-glycosides vitexin and isovitexin. Operating as a clean metabolic substrate, this functional food downregulates systemic postprandial glycemic excursions, promotes microvascular endothelial stability, and provides robust intracellular radical-scavenging activity.
macroIntro: The macronutrient architecture of cooked mung beans offers a highly bioavailable assembly of plant peptides linked with slowly hydrolyzable complex starches, ensuring extended satiety dynamics.
microIntro: A specialized micronutrient matrix abundant in critical single-carbon donors, structural enzyme activators, and highly functional embryonic seed polyphenols.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A functional matrix of soluble pectins and insoluble cellulose that optimizes intestinal transit and drives short-chain fatty acid production.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: A crucial intracellular divalent cation required for stabilizing metabolic enzymes and maintaining nerve signal transduction.

microNutrients.name: Vitexin and Isovitexin
microNutrients.description: Dominant seed-coat flavone C-glycosides that exert powerful anti-inflammatory effects and direct free-radical neutralization.

healthBenefits: Reduced Alpha-Galactoside Load and Gastrointestinal Comfort: The naturally low baseline of raffinose and stachyose oligosaccharides in Vigna radiata limits excessive substrate availability for colonic bacterial fermentation, minimizing luminal gas evolution and abdominal distension.

Amylose-Driven Postprandial Glucose Stabilization: The high amylose-to-amylopectin ratio coupled with intact resistant starches slows down pancreatic alpha-amylase degradation kinetics, delivering a smooth, low-velocity glucose influx into the portal vein.

Vitexin-Mediated Inhibition of Advanced Glycation End-Products: Native flavone C-glycosides interact directly with free amino groups to inhibit the structural cross-linking of proteins, preventing the formation of advanced glycation end-products.

Bile Acid Sequestration and Serum Cholesterol Management: The active soluble dietary fiber matrix forms a viscous intestinal gel that binds endogenic bile acids, forcing their fecal evacuation and accelerating the hepatic conversion of circulating cholesterol into new bile units.
precautionsIntro: Even though Vigna radiata presents a highly optimized digestibility profile, its physiological deployment requires structured attention under specific clinical states:
precautions: Phytic Acid Chelating Effects on Divalent Cations: Raw and improperly hydrated seeds contain phytic acid structures that can chelate free minerals like zinc and iron in the upper digestive tract, requiring adequate thermal processing or sprouting.

Protease Inhibitor Persistence in Incomplete Thermal Processing: Minor residual concentrations of Kunitz-type trypsin inhibitors can survive insufficient boiling, partially interfering with luminal protein degradation and causing mild digestive delay.

Mechanical Volumetric Pressure During Acute Gastrointestinal Inflammation: The substantial structural fiber mass can exert undesirable mechanical friction against hypersensitive mucosal layers during active phases of ulcerative colitis or gastritis.
